title: x402 settlement census — one DELTA between two rounds
description: What changed between two buyer's-eye rounds of the same population (x402-census-round-v1.json): which hosts returned a different outcome, what the doors asked, who they named as payee, and which hosts took a settlement and refused anyway. This is the artefact the round exists to produce — a listing does not move when a host stops answering paid requests, and this document is where that shows up. Produced only by scripts/grants/x402_census_delta.py from the two rounds' committed rows; `--check` recomputes it and fails on a single changed byte. It ranks nothing, recommends nothing and accuses nobody: REFUSED is indistinguishable from rate-limiting, an account requirement or changed terms when observed from outside. Every host row carries `observations` against `observations_required`, and `state` is UNMEASURED on every one of them until that threshold is met — a flip is an observation, never a verdict.

from.description: The earlier round. rows_sha256 pins the exact bytes compared, so a delta cannot silently be re-derived from different rows.

days_between.description: Derived from the two as_of stamps. A delta over an irregular gap is still a delta, but the gap is stated rather than assumed to be a week.

population_identical.description: True when both rounds carry the same population digest. When false, `hosts.added` and `hosts.dropped` say by how much — and a dropped host is NEVER counted as a flip: leaving the population is not a change of behaviour.

flipped.description: The headline. Only hosts present in BOTH rounds can flip. `transitions` is the full FROM->TO histogram, so the two named directions can never be mistaken for the whole picture.

held.description: Hosts whose outcome did not move. Published because a delta that lists only changes hides its own denominator.

price_drift.description: Change in the units the challenge asked for. Asset units exactly as the door stated them — never a currency figure of ours, never a tier, never a price this estate charges.

pay_to_changed.description: Hosts whose challenge names a different payee than it did last round. A fact about the door; not an allegation about anyone.

take_and_refuse.description: persisted / new / cleared across the pair. Persistence over rounds is the only thing that distinguishes a bad moment from a pattern, and even then the state stays UNMEASURED until n>=30.

receipts.description: Whether hosts returned a parseable settlement reference, each side of the pair.

ladder.description: The visible climb toward a publishable per-host state. Observations accrue one per round per host, so at a weekly cadence n=30 is roughly thirty weeks away — and this block says so numerically rather than letting a reader assume a flip means something settled.

rows_path.description: The per-host JSONL every count above was folded from.
